_: Read by scripts/gates/css_ownership.py. The rule is
docs/principles/domain-scoped-dependencies.md.
A stylesheet's domain is the domain of the directory it sits in, so the
path half of the census is scripts/domain-boundaries.json and is not
repeated here. This file answers the half a path cannot: which domain a
CSS class belongs to. Without it, removing a block leaves its styling
behind in substrate, because the domain-boundary gate reads TS imports and
a stylesheet has none.
`owners` maps a class-name prefix to a domain named in that census. A
class matches its prefix exactly or continues with `-` or `__`, so one
entry covers a BEM block with every element and modifier under it, and the
longest matching prefix wins. The gate constrains the stylesheet that
DECLARES a selector, never the markup that uses one: a block's component
may wear a substrate class such as `.set-row` exactly as it may render a
design-system component.
`shared` lists the prefixes that belong to no domain — design-system class
names the app qualifies (`.tab__close.icon-btn` is a delta over the DS
IconButton, not a second owner of it) and vendor class names. A shared
class never decides who owns a rule, and a rule built only from shared
classes has no owner at all, which the gate treats as a failure rather
than a pass.
